## Design

### 2026-10-25 – I started by familiarizing myself with KiCad. It was my first time using it, so I needed to download it which took some time. I then followed the instructions and finished the set up accordingly. It t

**4h**

I started by familiarizing myself with KiCad. It was my first time using it, so I needed to download it which took some time. I then followed the instructions and finished the set up accordingly. It took a lot of time just figuring out how they managed to put in the Waveshare thing and all this terminology is terribly new. After a lot of testing, I finally managed to get the Waveshare, the switches, the net labels, and more onto the board.

### 2026-10-25 – Since the last time I worked on this project, a lot has changed. I basically finished the rest in one sitting. I started by first finishing the schematics which was easier than I thought would be, but

**13h**

Since the last time I worked on this project, a lot has changed. I basically finished the rest in one sitting. I started by first finishing the schematics which was easier than I thought would be, but that was just the beginning. After, I moved on to assigning footprints which at that time, I thought probably would be the worst part I would experience. Well, I was definitely wrong. I had to download external plugins, and I had to deal with the wires not connecting to each other. My footprint design was also way too small and the boundaries restricted wiring from connecting to it. I spent 2 hours just figuring out why I couldn't reupdate the footprint, so I just created a new one and went from there. For the boundaries, I just switched to courtyard because I wasn't sure if it was made clear to use "courtyard" or "margins" for the border. After a full hour or so of wiring off of the reference image. In the end, I finally finished the project, and it was worth every second. I won't go into the details about how I built it because that would take forever. Just know that I built the schematic, assigned footprints, put it into the PCB editor, created a footprint, reupdated the footprint twice, and wired the whole thing together.
